verdicts.evidence: The logbook explicitly states that CalPro's actual architecture (geometric graph evidential head, differentiable conformal calibration layer, domain priors as soft constraints) was never implemented; the scripts used a 1-D synthetic regression closest to the paper's 'Evidential-only' ablation.

A text audit of Section 4 found the paper's own Sec. 4.3 says the Theorem 4.2 bound is 'agnostic to the presence of priors,' contradicting 'structure-aware,' and a numeric check (audit_thm42.py) showed L_s*epsilon=39.47 making the coverage bound vacuous—but the numeric check ran on a synthetic 1-D regression, not real protein data.

No experiments on held-out X-ray protein structures were run; the ECE numbers reported (0.0113 in-distribution, 0.1050 shifted) come from a synthetic heteroscedastic regression and do not match or address the claimed 90.1% coverage / 0.021 ECE on protein structures.

The logbook explicitly withdraws its earlier verdict and states A4 is 'NOT TESTED': the synthetic covariate-shift experiment used no proteins, no cryo-EM modality shift, no pLDDT baseline, and no CalPro method.
The logbook marks this claim 'OUT OF SCOPE (not attempted)'—no docking pipeline, no protein structures, and no filtering experiments were executed.

ECE was tested on synthetic heteroscedastic regression (81.5% reduction in-distribution, 26.4% under shift), but the 0.83 Spearman correlation and near-nominal coverage across real modalities were not tested; the setup is a synthetic proxy, not protein structures.

overall: The logbook's main substantive finding is a theoretical audit of Theorem 4.2 showing the paper's own text contradicts the 'structure-aware' framing and a synthetic numeric check demonstrating the bound goes vacuous, but none of the paper's core protein-structure, modality-shift, or docking claims were tested on real data. The logbook honestly withdraws an earlier invalid verdict on the modality-shift claim and correctly flags most protein-specific claims as untested.
